newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Mercedes sees higher 1997 truck production.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes sees higher 1997 truck production.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG truck production is likely to climb slightly to over 350,000 units in 1997 from around 348,200 units last year, truck unit chief Kurt Lauk said on Friday.
Speaking at a truck show here, Lauk said the the unit was also positioned to offer higher profits and that by the end of the decade the unit would be able to make a profit in all its operations.
In 1996, unit truck sales climbed to 348,200 units from 320,100 units while revenue slipped to 31.5 million marks ($19.7 million) from 31.6 million marks, Lauk said.
Sales were helped last year by the company's light trucks and vans.
Mercedes has been hit especially hard by weak European demand for heavy trucks and has seen its market share slip in that sector in recent years, analysts said.
Mercedes director Kurt Lauk said at the truck fair here that the 12 percent goal matched that of the Daimler group.
Mercedes 1996 truck sales totaled 31.5 billion marks.
